title: Ulyana and the Harbor
premise: In 1899, Zephyrine Iversen, a mapmaker's apprentice quietly completing the atlas his dead master sacrificed everything for, lives invisibly among the harbor folk of Ulyana. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Iversen family as conspirators in a smuggling plot they never joined, Zephyrine must abandon his careful anonymity to clear their name. As the port authorities close in and the last emigrant ship of the century prepares to sail, he uncovers the truth: the real conspirator is the harbormaster who forged the letter to seize the Iversen shipping routes. In the end, Zephyrine exposes the plot at the cost of the atlas, and must choose which family member — his ailing grandmother or his young brother — takes the final berth aboard the departing ship before the century turns.
about_author: Coral Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime maps in northern coastal towns. She writes historical fiction about the quiet people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coastline
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He works late finishing the master's atlas, tracing a coastline the old man died surveying, while keeping his head down in the harbor town of Ulyana. Introduces his found family of dockworkers and his grandmother's boarding house. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into devotion, and the comfort of small routines.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A government courier delivers a sealed letter naming the Iversen family in a smuggling conspiracy. Zephyrine burns it — then finds an identical copy already posted on the customs house door. Emotional beat: the sick drop of realizing anonymity was always borrowed, never owned.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Grandmother Sigrid's POV. She reviews the family's shipping ledgers, certain someone has been forging entries in her hand. She says nothing to the children, protecting them as she always has. Emotional beat: fierce maternal love shadowed by guilt over secrets she kept during the famine years.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Harbormaster Voss visits the boarding house with false courtesy, offering to make the investigation 'disappear' if the family signs over their berth rights. Zephyrine notices Voss's cufflinks match wax seals on the accusatory letters. Emotional beat: first cold recognition of the enemy.

chapters.title: Little Brother's Map
chapters.summary: Anders, age eleven, POV. The boy draws imaginary maps like his brother taught him and overhears dockworkers whispering that the Iversens will be run out by New Year's. He hides what he heard. Emotional beat: childhood innocence straining against dawning fear.

chapters.title: Salt and Testimony
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He interviews sailors his master once surveyed with, piecing together that cargo manifests were altered the night the master drowned. A drunk boatswain confirms Voss ordered the route change. Emotional beat: the thrill of purpose replacing years of self-erasure.

chapters.title: What Sigrid Buried
chapters.summary: Sigrid's POV. She digs up a tin box containing proof she once smuggled grain to starving families — the very crime now pinned on them. She decides to confess alone if it comes to it. Emotional beat: a mother's arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He seeks out Lene, the master's estranged daughter, who holds half the atlas's source documents. Their wary collaboration kindles into something warmer as they compare notes by lamplight. Emotional beat: two lonely people discovering they are not alone.

chapters.title: Customs House Fire
chapters.summary: Anders' POV. A fire guts the customs archive the night before the family's hearing; Anders sees Voss's clerk leaving with a satchel but tells no one, terrified. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of knowledge a child shouldn't carry.

chapters.title: Hearing Before the Magistrate
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. With the archives burned, the hearing goes badly; the magistrate suspends the family's berthing license. Zephyrine nearly reveals the tin box's contents but Sigrid silences him with a look. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Lene's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lene's POV. She offers the magistrate her father's original survey journals as evidence, demanding protection for the Iversens in exchange. The magistrate hesitates — Voss has friends above him. Emotional beat: courage offered freely, and its limits.

chapters.title: The Last Berth Announced
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The emigrant ship Meridian announces its final sailing of the century; one berth remains in the Iversen name, transferable to any family member. The household falls silent around the supper table. Emotional beat: hope and heartbreak arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Everyone Volunteers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. Anders wants to go for adventure; Sigrid insists the boy should have her place; Zephyrine argues the berth should be sold to fund their defense. Each secret motive surfaces. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument, each trying to be the one who leaves.

chapters.title: Night Survey
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Lene's POV, alternating. They sneak into the flooded quarry where the master drowned, recovering his hidden field case from beneath the ice shelf. Inside: the true manifests and a map marking Voss's cache. Emotional beat: completing the dead man's work as an act of love.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Feeling the net tighten, he orders the Iversen warehouse seized and has Zephyrine followed. He justifies everything as order against chaos. Emotional beat: chilling banality of a man who believes himself reasonable.

chapters.title: The Tin Box Opens
chapters.summary: Sigrid's POV. Confronted by Zephyrine, she finally opens the tin box and tells the truth of the famine winters. He realizes the forged ledger entries mimic her old handwriting because Voss learned it from her, decades ago. Emotional beat: shame met with absolution.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The follower turns out to be Tomas, a dockworker Zephyrine considered family, paid in debt relief. Tomas warns him instead of reporting him — but Voss learns of the quarry recovery anyway. Emotional beat: found family fractured and mended in a single night.

chapters.title: Century's Eve
chapters.summary: Anders' POV. On December 31st, the town prepares fireworks while soldiers seal the harbor. Anders slips the recovered manifests into the magistrate's sleigh, doing the brave thing he'd been too scared to do before. Emotional beat: a child choosing courage.

chapters.title: The Meridian Departs
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the gangplank, with minutes left, Zephyrine makes the choice: he gives the berth to Sigrid, knowing she'll refuse it — and she does, pressing it to Anders, who boards weeping, waving until the ship is a speck. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of love, resolved.

chapters.title: Voss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Climax. Zephyrine's POV. At the New Year's assembly, the manifests and Lene's testimony land before the magistrate as Voss moves to arrest the family. The crowd of dockworkers — Zephyrine's found family — stands as witnesses. Voss is taken in irons. Emotional beat: cathartic reckoning.

chapters.title: The Atlas Completed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He inks the final plate of the atlas and, at Lene's urging, signs both their names beside the master's. The magistrate offers him the official cartographer's post. Emotional beat: a man who hid for years stepping into the light, named at last.

chapters.title: Home Water
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring 1900. Anders writes from across the sea; Sigrid plants a garden; Lene and Zephyrine chart the harbor anew. The boarding house fills with new arrivals needing a place. Emotional beat: belonging not found but built, open-door and ongoing.
